title.hg: Sab Alag Hain, Sab Apne Hain

subtitle.en: Families, toys, games and being kind

hook.en: No two people are the same. That is what makes a class, a family and a playground fun.
hook.hg: Koi bhi do log ek jaise nahi hote. Isi se toh class, family aur playground mazedaar banta hai.

objectives.en: Say that people look, speak and live in different ways, and that this is okay.
objectives.hg: Bata sako ki log alag dikhte hain, alag bolte hain aur alag tarah se rehte hain, aur yeh theek hai.

objectives.en: Know that toys, colours, games and jobs are for everyone.
objectives.hg: Jaan sako ki khilone, colours, games aur jobs sabke liye hain.

objectives.en: Know what to do when someone is being teased.
objectives.hg: Jaan sako ki jab kisi ko chidhaya jaye toh kya karna hai.

body.en: Look around your class. Some children are tall and some are short. Some speak Hindi at home, some speak Tamil, Bengali or English. Some wear glasses. Some use a wheelchair or a hearing aid. Some talk a lot and some are quiet. Different is not bad. Different is normal.
body.hg: Apni class mein chaaron taraf dekho. Koi baccha lamba hai, koi chhota. Koi ghar pe Hindi bolta hai, koi Tamil, Bengali ya English. Koi chashma pehenta hai. Koi wheelchair ya hearing aid use karta hai. Koi bahut bolta hai, koi chup rehta hai. Alag hona bura nahi hai. Alag hona bilkul normal hai.

h.hg: Families kai tarah ki hoti hain

body.en: Families come in many shapes. Some children live with a mother and a father. Some live with only one parent, or with grandparents, an aunt or an uncle. Some children are adopted. Some have two homes. Some families are big and some are small. What makes a family is love and care.
body.hg: Families kai tarah ki hoti hain. Kuch bacche mummy aur papa dono ke saath rehte hain. Kuch sirf mummy ya sirf papa ke saath, ya dada-dadi, nana-nani, mausi ya chacha ke saath. Kuch bacche adopt kiye gaye hain. Kuch ke do ghar hote hain. Koi family badi hai, koi chhoti. Family pyaar aur dekhbhaal se banti hai.

h.en: Toys, colours, games and jobs are for everyone
h.hg: Khilone, colours, games aur jobs sabke liye hain

body.en: There are no boy colours and no girl colours. Pink, blue, yellow and green are for anyone. Girls can play cricket and boys can play with dolls and kitchen sets. Anyone can grow up to be a doctor, a pilot, a chef, a teacher or a nurse. You choose what you like.
body.hg: Koi colour ladkon ka ya ladkiyon ka nahi hota. Pink, blue, yellow aur green sabke liye hain. Ladkiyan cricket khel sakti hain aur ladke gudiya aur kitchen set se khel sakte hain. Bada hokar koi bhi doctor, pilot, chef, teacher ya nurse ban sakta hai. Tumhe jo pasand hai, woh tum chuno.

body.en: Teasing someone for how they look, talk, dress or play hurts them. If you see it, do not laugh. You can say, 'Stop. That is not kind.' Then go and stand with that child. If the teasing does not stop, tell a teacher or a grown-up you trust.
body.hg: Kisi ko uske dikhne, bolne, kapdon ya khelne ke tareeke pe chidhane se use dukh hota hai. Agar tum aisa hote dekho, toh hanso mat. Tum bol sakte ho, 'Ruko. Yeh achhi baat nahi hai.' Phir us bacche ke paas jaakar khade ho jao. Agar chidhana band na ho, toh teacher ko ya kisi bharose wale bade ko batao.

claim.en: Boys should not cry and girls should not get dirty while playing.
claim.hg: Ladkon ko rona nahi chahiye aur ladkiyon ko khelte hue ganda nahi hona chahiye.

fact.en: Everyone has feelings, so everyone can cry. Everyone can run, climb and play in the mud. Feelings and games are for all children.
fact.hg: Feelings sabme hoti hain, isliye ro koi bhi sakta hai. Daudna, chadhna aur mitti mein khelna bhi sabke liye hai. Feelings aur games sab bacchon ke hain.

takeaways.en: Being different is normal and makes the world interesting.
takeaways.hg: Alag hona normal hai aur isi se duniya interesting banti hai.

takeaways.en: Every kind of family that gives love and care is a real family.
takeaways.hg: Pyaar aur care dene wali har tarah ki family asli family hai.

takeaways.en: Toys, colours, games and jobs are for everyone, and teasing is never okay.
takeaways.hg: Khilone, colours, games aur jobs sabke liye hain, aur kisi ko chidhana kabhi theek nahi.

activity.en: Draw your family. Then draw one thing that makes you different from your best friend and one thing you both like.
activity.hg: Apni family ki drawing banao. Phir ek aisi cheez banao jo tumhe apne best friend se alag banati hai, aur ek aisi cheez jo tum dono ko pasand hai.

q.en: Who can play with a kitchen set?
q.hg: Kitchen set se kaun khel sakta hai?

options.en: Only girls
options.hg: Sirf ladkiyan

options.en: Only boys
options.hg: Sirf ladke

options.en: Anyone who likes it
options.hg: Jise bhi pasand ho

explain.en: Toys are for everyone. Any child can play with what they like.
explain.hg: Khilone sabke liye hain. Har baccha apni pasand ki cheez se khel sakta hai.

q.en: A family is only real if it has a mother and a father.
q.hg: Family tabhi asli hoti hai jab usme mummy aur papa dono hon.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: Families come in many kinds. Love and care make a family, not the number of parents.
explain.hg: Families kai tarah ki hoti hain. Family pyaar aur care se banti hai, parents ki ginti se nahi.

title.en: Who Made These Rules? Gender Stereotypes
title.hg: Ye Rules Kisne Banaye? Gender Stereotypes

subtitle.en: Why 'boys don't cry' and 'girls can't' are ideas, not facts
subtitle.hg: 'Ladke rote nahi' aur 'ladkiyan nahi kar sakti' sirf soch hai, fact nahi

hook.en: 'Boys don't cry.' 'Girls don't play cricket.' Nobody voted for these rules, yet people repeat them every day.
hook.hg: 'Ladke rote nahi.' 'Ladkiyan cricket nahi khelti.' In rules pe kabhi kisi ne vote nahi diya, phir bhi log roz inhe repeat karte hain.

objectives.en: Explain what a gender stereotype is.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki gender stereotype kya hota hai.

objectives.en: Give examples of how stereotypes limit both girls and boys.
objectives.hg: Examples de sako ki stereotypes ladkiyon aur ladkon dono ko kaise rokte hain.

objectives.en: Respond calmly and respectfully when someone is teased for not fitting a stereotype.
objectives.hg: Jab kisi ko stereotype mein fit na hone pe chidhaya jaye, toh calmly aur respect se jawab de sako.

body.en: A stereotype is a fixed idea about a whole group of people, as if everyone in the group must be the same. A gender stereotype says what boys 'should' be like and what girls 'should' be like. For example: boys are strong and good at maths, girls are gentle and good at cooking. These ideas are not facts about bodies or brains. They are habits that people pick up from family, films, advertisements, textbooks and friends. Because we hear them so often, they start to sound true. They are still only ideas, and ideas can be questioned.
body.hg: Stereotype matlab logon ke poore group ke baare mein ek fixed bani-banayi soch, jaise us group ka har insaan same hi hoga. Gender stereotype batata hai ki ladkon ko kaisa 'hona chahiye' aur ladkiyon ko kaisa 'hona chahiye'. Jaise: ladke strong hote hain aur maths mein achhe, ladkiyan soft hoti hain aur cooking mein achhi. Ye baatein body ya brain ke baare mein koi fact nahi hain. Ye aadatein hain jo log family, films, ads, textbooks aur doston se seekh lete hain. Baar-baar sunne se ye sach jaisi lagne lagti hain. Phir bhi ye sirf ideas hain, aur ideas pe sawaal uthaya ja sakta hai.

h.hg: Stereotypes sabko kaise hurt karte hain

body.en: Stereotypes put people in boxes. A girl who loves football may be told to 'sit properly and play inside'. A boy who loves dance or drawing may be laughed at. Boys are often told not to cry, so many learn to hide sadness and fear, and those feelings come out as anger instead. Girls are often told to stay quiet, so many stop sharing their opinions in class. In both cases a child loses something they are good at or something they need. Nobody chose their box, and nobody fits inside one perfectly.
body.hg: Stereotypes logon ko boxes mein daal dete hain. Jis ladki ko football pasand hai, use bola ja sakta hai 'dhang se baitho aur andar khelo'. Jis ladke ko dance ya drawing pasand hai, uspe log hans sakte hain. Ladkon ko aksar bola jata hai ki rona nahi hai, toh kai ladke sadness aur darr chhupana seekh jaate hain, aur wahi feelings gussa bankar bahar aati hain. Ladkiyon ko aksar chup rehne ko bola jata hai, toh kai ladkiyan class mein apni opinion dena chhod deti hain. Dono cases mein baccha kuch aisa kho deta hai jisme woh achha hai ya jiski use zaroorat hai. Apna box kisi ne khud nahi chuna, aur koi bhi usme perfectly fit nahi hota.

h.en: Equality starts at home and school
h.hg: Equality ghar aur school se shuru hoti hai

body.en: Gender equality means every child gets the same respect, chances and responsibilities. It does not mean everyone must be identical. Look at ordinary days. Who is asked to serve water to guests? Who gets more time to play outside? Who is told to study science and who is told to 'adjust'? Fair looks like this: brothers and sisters share the housework, everyone gets equal food, study time and play time, and the class monitor, the team captain or the science-fair leader can be any child who is ready for the job.
body.hg: Gender equality ka matlab hai har bacche ko same respect, same chances aur same responsibilities milein. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki sab ek jaise ho jayein. Roz ki cheezon pe dhyaan do. Guests ko paani dene ke liye kise bulaya jata hai? Bahar khelne ka zyada time kise milta hai? Science padhne ko kise bola jata hai aur 'adjust kar lo' kise bola jata hai? Fair aisa dikhta hai: bhai-behen ghar ka kaam milke karte hain, sabko barabar khana, study time aur play time milta hai, aur class monitor, team captain ya science fair ka leader koi bhi baccha ban sakta hai jo us kaam ke liye ready ho.

body.en: When someone says 'that's for girls' or 'be a man', you do not have to fight. A calm line works better. Try: 'Says who?' or 'Anyone can like that.' or 'I cry when I'm sad, same as everybody.' If a classmate is being teased, do not join the laughing. Stand next to them, change the topic, or say 'Leave it, yaar.' If the teasing keeps happening, turns into name-calling, or moves to a class group chat, tell a teacher or parent. Reporting bullying is not complaining. It is how it stops.
body.hg: Jab koi bole 'yeh toh ladkiyon wala hai' ya 'mard ban', toh ladne ki zaroorat nahi. Calm si ek line zyada kaam karti hai. Try karo: 'Kisne bola?' ya 'Yeh kisi ko bhi pasand ho sakta hai.' ya 'Dukh hota hai toh mujhe rona aata hai, jaise sabko aata hai.' Agar kisi classmate ko chidhaya ja raha ho, toh hansne walon mein shaamil mat ho. Uske paas jaake khade ho jao, topic change kar do, ya bolo 'Chhod na yaar.' Agar teasing baar-baar ho, gande naam rakhne tak pahunch jaye, ya class ke group chat mein hone lage, toh teacher ya parents ko batao. Bullying report karna complain karna nahi hai. Isi se woh rukti hai.

claim.en: Boys are naturally strong and girls are naturally weak.
claim.hg: Ladke naturally strong hote hain aur ladkiyan naturally weak.

fact.en: Strength depends on the person: their age, food, health and practice, not only on being a boy or a girl. In childhood, girls and boys are quite similar in strength, and at every age there are strong girls and gentle boys. Courage and kindness belong to everyone.
fact.hg: Strength insaan pe depend karti hai: uski age, khana, health aur practice pe, sirf ladka ya ladki hone pe nahi. Bachpan mein ladkiyon aur ladkon ki strength kaafi milti-julti hoti hai, aur har age mein strong ladkiyan aur gentle ladke hote hain. Himmat aur kindness sabki hoti hai.

takeaways.en: A gender stereotype is a learned idea about what boys or girls 'should' be, not a fact.
takeaways.hg: Gender stereotype ek seekhi hui soch hai ki ladkon ya ladkiyon ko kaisa 'hona chahiye', yeh fact nahi hai.

takeaways.en: Stereotypes take away choices from girls and from boys.
takeaways.hg: Stereotypes ladkiyon aur ladkon dono se unki choices chheen lete hain.

takeaways.en: Equality means equal respect, chances and chores, and you can speak up calmly for it.
takeaways.hg: Equality matlab barabar respect, barabar chances aur barabar kaam, aur iske liye tum calmly bol sakte ho.

activity.en: Be a stereotype detective for one day. Note three ads, cartoons or sentences that say what boys or girls 'should' do. Next to each, write the name of one real person you know who breaks that rule.
activity.hg: Ek din ke liye stereotype detective bano. Teen aise ads, cartoons ya sentences note karo jo batate hain ki ladkon ya ladkiyon ko kya 'karna chahiye'. Har ek ke aage kisi aise real insaan ka naam likho jise tum jaante ho aur jo woh rule todta hai.

q.en: Which of these is a gender stereotype?
q.hg: Inme se kaun-sa gender stereotype hai?

options.en: Some girls in my class like cricket.
options.hg: Meri class ki kuch ladkiyon ko cricket pasand hai.

options.en: All boys are bad at cooking.
options.hg: Saare ladke cooking mein kacche hote hain.

options.en: My sister is taller than me.
options.hg: Meri behen mujhse lambi hai.

options.en: Rohan cried when his dog was sick.
options.hg: Jab Rohan ka dog bimaar tha toh woh roya.

explain.en: A stereotype claims that everyone in a group is the same. The other sentences describe particular people.
explain.hg: Stereotype yeh claim karta hai ki group ka har insaan same hai. Baaki sentences kisi particular insaan ke baare mein hain.

q.en: During a match, Kabir falls and starts crying. A teammate says, 'Stop crying like a girl.' What is the best thing to say?
q.hg: Match ke dauraan Kabir gir jata hai aur rone lagta hai. Ek teammate bolta hai, 'Ladkiyon ki tarah rona band kar.' Best jawab kya hoga?

options.en: 'Anyone cries when it hurts. Kabir, are you okay?'
options.hg: 'Chot lage toh koi bhi rota hai. Kabir, tu theek hai?'

options.en: 'Yes Kabir, be a man.'
options.hg: 'Haan Kabir, mard ban.'

options.en: Say nothing and laugh along so that nobody teases you.
options.hg: Kuch mat bolo aur saath mein hans do taaki tumhe koi na chidhaye.

explain.en: It corrects the stereotype without a fight and checks on Kabir. Crying when hurt is normal for every child.
explain.hg: Yeh jawab bina jhagde ke stereotype ko correct karta hai aur Kabir ka haal bhi poochta hai. Chot lagne pe rona har bacche ke liye normal hai.

title.en: Sex, Gender, Attraction: Four Different Things
title.hg: Sex, Gender, Attraction: Chaar Alag Cheezein

subtitle.en: Biological sex, gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation, untangled
subtitle.hg: Biological sex, gender identity, gender expression aur sexual orientation ko alag-alag samjho

hook.en: People mix up these four words all the time. Once you separate them, most of the confusion about gender and sexuality disappears.
hook.hg: Log in chaar words ko hamesha mix kar dete hain. Inhe alag-alag samajh lo, toh gender aur sexuality ka zyadatar confusion khatam ho jata hai.

objectives.en: Tell apart biological sex, gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation.
objectives.hg: Biological sex, gender identity, gender expression aur sexual orientation mein farak bata sako.

objectives.en: Explain that intersex variations and diverse identities are natural, not illnesses.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki intersex variations aur alag-alag identities natural hain, bimaari nahi.

objectives.en: Know that there is no deadline for putting a label on yourself.
objectives.hg: Jaan sako ki khud pe label lagane ki koi deadline nahi hoti.

body.en: Biological sex describes body features: chromosomes (often XX or XY), hormones, internal reproductive organs and external genitals. At birth a doctor looks at the baby's genitals and records 'female' or 'male'. This is called sex assigned at birth. Bodies do not always fall neatly into two types. Some people are born with chromosomes, hormones or anatomy that do not match the typical definitions of male or female. These are called intersex variations. They are natural variations of the human body, not a disease and not anyone's fault. Some are noticed at birth, some at puberty, and some are never noticed at all.
body.hg: Biological sex body ke features ke baare mein hai: chromosomes (aksar XX ya XY), hormones, andar ke reproductive organs aur bahar ke genitals. Birth ke time doctor baby ke genitals dekhkar 'female' ya 'male' likh dete hain. Isse sex assigned at birth kehte hain. Bodies hamesha neatly do hi types mein nahi aati. Kuch log aise chromosomes, hormones ya anatomy ke saath paida hote hain jo male ya female ki typical definition se match nahi karti. Inhe intersex variations kehte hain. Ye human body ki natural variations hain, na koi bimaari aur na kisi ki galti. Kuch birth pe pata chalti hain, kuch puberty mein, aur kuch ka kabhi pata hi nahi chalta.

h.en: Gender identity: who you know yourself to be
h.hg: Gender identity: tum khud ko kya jaante ho

body.en: Gender identity is a person's own inner sense of being a girl or woman, a boy or man, both, neither, or somewhere in between. For most people it matches the sex recorded at birth; the word for this is cisgender. For some people it does not match; the word is transgender. Some people do not feel fully like a man or a woman and may use the word non-binary. South Asia has long had communities such as hijra and kinnar, so gender diversity is neither new nor foreign to India. You cannot see someone's identity from outside. The respectful way to know is to listen to what they tell you.
body.hg: Gender identity kisi insaan ka apne andar ka ehsaas hai ki woh ladki ya woman hai, ladka ya man hai, dono hai, koi nahi hai, ya kahin beech mein hai. Zyadatar logon mein yeh birth pe likhe gaye sex se match karta hai; iske liye word hai cisgender. Kuch logon mein match nahi karta; iske liye word hai transgender. Kuch log khud ko poori tarah man ya woman feel nahi karte aur non-binary word use kar sakte hain. South Asia mein hijra aur kinnar jaise communities bahut purane time se hain, toh gender diversity India ke liye na nayi hai, na bahar se aayi hai. Kisi ki identity bahar se dekhkar pata nahi chalti. Jaanne ka respectful tareeka yahi hai ki woh jo bataye, use suno.

h.en: Gender expression: how you show up
h.hg: Gender expression: tum khud ko kaise present karte ho

body.en: Gender expression is how a person presents themselves: clothes, hair, jewellery, voice, the way they walk or sit. Society labels these 'masculine' or 'feminine', but the labels change with time and place. Men in many parts of India wear a lungi, a dhoti or long hair, and nobody finds that unusual. Expression is not a clue to anything else. A boy who likes kajal or kathak is not automatically gay or transgender. A girl with short hair who rides a bike is not 'trying to be a boy'. Expression only tells you what someone likes to wear and do.
body.hg: Gender expression matlab insaan khud ko kaise present karta hai: kapde, baal, jewellery, awaaz, chalne ya baithne ka style. Society inpe 'masculine' ya 'feminine' ka label laga deti hai, par ye labels time aur jagah ke saath badalte rehte hain. India ke kai hisson mein men lungi, dhoti pehente hain ya lambe baal rakhte hain, aur kisi ko yeh ajeeb nahi lagta. Expression kisi aur cheez ka clue nahi hai. Jis ladke ko kajal ya kathak pasand hai, woh automatically gay ya transgender nahi ho jata. Chhote baalon wali ladki jo bike chalati hai, woh 'ladka banne ki koshish' nahi kar rahi. Expression se bas itna pata chalta hai ki kisi ko kya pehenna aur kya karna pasand hai.

h.en: Sexual orientation: who you are drawn to
h.hg: Sexual orientation: tum kiski taraf attract hote ho

body.en: Sexual orientation describes who a person feels romantic or sexual attraction to. Heterosexual (straight) means attraction to a different gender. Gay and lesbian mean attraction to the same gender. Bisexual means attraction to more than one gender. Asexual means feeling little or no sexual attraction. Orientation is not chosen, and nobody is 'turned' gay by friends, films or a phone. It is about feelings, not about anything a person has done. In your teens, crushes can be confusing and can shift. A crush on a friend of the same gender does not force any label on you. There is no deadline to decide, and you may keep it private.
body.hg: Sexual orientation batata hai ki kisi insaan ko romantic ya sexual attraction kiski taraf feel hota hai. Heterosexual (straight) matlab doosre gender ki taraf attraction. Gay aur lesbian matlab apne hi gender ki taraf attraction. Bisexual matlab ek se zyada gender ki taraf attraction. Asexual matlab sexual attraction bahut kam ya bilkul feel na hona. Orientation koi choose nahi karta, aur doston, films ya phone se koi gay 'ban' nahi jata. Yeh feelings ki baat hai, is baat ki nahi ki kisi ne kya kiya hai. Teens mein crushes confusing ho sakte hain aur shift bhi ho sakte hain. Apne hi gender ke kisi friend pe crush hone se tumpe koi label nahi lag jata. Decide karne ki koi deadline nahi hai, aur tum isse private rakh sakte ho.

claim.en: A transgender person and a gay person are the same thing.
claim.hg: Transgender hona aur gay hona ek hi baat hai.

fact.en: They are different. Being transgender is about gender identity, meaning who you are. Being gay, lesbian or bisexual is about sexual orientation, meaning who you are attracted to. A transgender person can be straight, gay, bisexual or asexual, like anyone else.
fact.hg: Ye do alag cheezein hain. Transgender hona gender identity ki baat hai, yaani tum kaun ho. Gay, lesbian ya bisexual hona sexual orientation ki baat hai, yaani tumhe attraction kiski taraf hota hai. Ek transgender insaan straight, gay, bisexual ya asexual, kuch bhi ho sakta hai, jaise koi bhi aur insaan.

takeaways.en: Sex is about the body, gender identity is who you are, expression is how you present, and orientation is who you are attracted to.
takeaways.hg: Sex body ki baat hai, gender identity yeh hai ki tum kaun ho, expression yeh hai ki tum khud ko kaise present karte ho, aur orientation yeh hai ki tumhe attraction kiski taraf hota hai.

takeaways.en: You cannot work out any one of the four from the other three.
takeaways.hg: In chaaron mein se kisi ek ka andaza baaki teen ko dekhkar nahi lagaya ja sakta.

takeaways.en: Being LGBTQ+ or intersex is part of natural human diversity, not an illness.
takeaways.hg: LGBTQ+ ya intersex hona insaano ki natural diversity ka hissa hai, koi bimaari nahi.

activity.en: In a private notebook, write the four terms as headings. Under each, write in your own words one thing you learned today. You do not need to write anything about yourself.
activity.hg: Apni private notebook mein chaaron terms ko headings ki tarah likho. Har ek ke neeche apne words mein aaj seekhi hui ek baat likho. Apne baare mein kuch bhi likhna zaroori nahi hai.

q.hg: Sexual orientation kis baare mein hai?

options.en: the clothes and hairstyle a person prefers
options.hg: insaan ko kaise kapde aur hairstyle pasand hain

options.en: the sex written on a person's birth record
options.hg: insaan ke birth record mein likha sex

options.en: who a person feels romantic or sexual attraction to
options.hg: insaan ko romantic ya sexual attraction kiski taraf feel hota hai

options.en: whether a person behaves in a masculine or feminine way
options.hg: insaan ka behaviour masculine hai ya feminine

explain.en: Orientation is about attraction. Clothes and behaviour are gender expression, and the birth record is sex assigned at birth.
explain.hg: Orientation attraction ki baat hai. Kapde aur behaviour gender expression hain, aur birth record sex assigned at birth hai.

q.en: You can tell a person's gender identity by looking at their clothes.
q.hg: Kisi ke kapde dekhkar uski gender identity batayi ja sakti hai.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: Clothes are gender expression. Identity is an inner sense that only the person can tell you about.
explain.hg: Kapde gender expression hain. Identity andar ka ehsaas hai, jiske baare mein sirf wahi insaan bata sakta hai.

title.en: Discrimination, the Law and Your Mind

subtitle.en: What gender and LGBTQ+ discrimination looks like in India, what the law says, and how to protect your wellbeing
subtitle.hg: India mein gender aur LGBTQ+ discrimination kaisa dikhta hai, law kya kehta hai, aur apni wellbeing kaise protect karein

hook.en: Identity does not damage mental health. Being mocked, hidden, controlled or thrown out for it does.
hook.hg: Identity se mental health kharab nahi hoti. Kharab hoti hai us identity ke liye mazaak udaye jaane, chhupne pe majboor hone, control kiye jaane ya ghar se nikale jaane se.

objectives.en: Recognise gender discrimination in everyday situations.
objectives.hg: Roz ki situations mein gender discrimination ko pehchaan sako.

objectives.en: Describe in plain language where Indian law stands on same-sex relationships and transgender rights.
objectives.hg: Simple language mein bata sako ki same-sex relationships aur transgender rights pe Indian law kya kehta hai.

objectives.en: Explain why stigma, not identity, harms mental health, and where support is available.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki mental health ko nuksaan identity se nahi, stigma se hota hai, aur support kahan milta hai.

body.en: Gender discrimination means treating someone worse because of their gender. Much of it looks ordinary. A daughter's education is stopped earlier than a son's. Girls get curfews while boys get freedom. A woman is paid less for the same work, or asked in an interview when she plans to marry. A boy is mocked for choosing nursing or fashion design. A transgender person is refused a rented room, a job or respectful treatment at a hospital. Preferring sons over daughters is the same thing at its most serious. None of this is 'just tradition'. Each example takes a real opportunity away from a real person.
body.hg: Gender discrimination matlab kisi ke saath uske gender ki wajah se bura ya kamtar treatment karna. Iska bada hissa bilkul ordinary lagta hai. Beti ki padhai bete se pehle chhudwa di jaati hai. Ladkiyon pe curfew hota hai aur ladkon ko freedom. Woman ko same kaam ke kam paise milte hain, ya interview mein poocha jata hai ki shaadi kab karogi. Ladke ka mazaak udta hai kyunki usne nursing ya fashion design choose kiya. Transgender insaan ko rent ka kamra, job ya hospital mein respectful treatment dene se mana kar diya jata hai. Betiyon ki jagah beton ko prefer karna isi discrimination ka sabse serious roop hai. Inme se kuch bhi 'bas tradition' nahi hai. Har example mein ek real insaan se ek real opportunity chhinti hai.

body.en: In 2014 the Supreme Court recognised transgender persons' right to identify their own gender and to equal constitutional rights. In 2018 it ruled that consensual same-sex relations between adults are not a crime. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 prohibits discrimination in education, employment, healthcare and housing. A 2026 amendment removed the Act's right to self-perceived gender identity, narrowed who it counts as transgender and tied identity certificates to a medical board; the Court is hearing challenges. In 2023 the Court declined to recognise same-sex marriage, leaving that to Parliament, so same-sex couples cannot currently register a marriage. Laws change; this is general information, not legal advice.
body.hg: 2014 mein Supreme Court ne maana ki transgender logon ko apna gender khud identify karne ka aur Constitution ke barabar rights ka haq hai. 2018 mein usne faisla diya ki adults ke beech consent se bane same-sex relations crime nahi hain. Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 education, employment, healthcare aur housing mein discrimination pe rok lagata hai. 2026 ke ek amendment ne is Act se self-perceived gender identity ka right hata diya, yeh narrow kar diya ki Act kise transgender maanta hai, aur identity certificate ko medical board se jod diya; is amendment ke khilaaf challenges Supreme Court sun raha hai. 2023 mein Court ne same-sex marriage ko legal recognition dene se mana kiya aur yeh decision Parliament pe chhod diya, isliye abhi India mein same-sex couples apni shaadi register nahi kara sakte. Laws badalte rehte hain, aur yeh general information hai, legal advice nahi.

h.en: Stigma is the injury, not identity
h.hg: Chot identity se nahi, stigma se lagti hai

body.en: Being lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, asexual or intersex is not a mental illness and needs no cure. Yet LGBTQ+ young people, and people who break gender rules, report more anxiety, low mood and thoughts of self-harm than their peers. Researchers link this to what they face: bullying, rejection at home, constant hiding and fear of being found out. This is sometimes called minority stress. The pattern also runs the other way: acceptance from family, a teacher or a friend is linked with better mental health. 'Conversion therapy' that claims to change orientation or identity has no scientific basis, causes harm, and is treated as professional misconduct for doctors in India.
body.hg: Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, asexual ya intersex hona koi mental illness nahi hai aur isse kisi ilaaj ki zaroorat nahi. Phir bhi LGBTQ+ young log, aur woh log jo gender ke rules todte hain, apne peers ke comparison mein zyada anxiety, low mood aur self-harm ke thoughts report karte hain. Researchers isse us treatment se jodte hain jo unhe jhelna padta hai: bullying, ghar mein rejection, lagataar chhupke rehna aur doosron ko pata chal jaane ka darr. Isse kabhi-kabhi minority stress kehte hain. Yahi pattern ulti direction mein bhi chalta hai: family, kisi teacher ya dost ka accept karna better mental health se juda hai. Orientation ya identity badalne ka claim karne wali 'conversion therapy' ka koi scientific basis nahi hai, yeh harm karti hai, aur India mein doctors ke liye isse professional misconduct maana jata hai.

h.en: Looking after yourself and each other

body.en: You never owe anyone a disclosure. Telling people about your identity, often called coming out, is your decision, made on your timeline, and safety comes first. If home may turn hostile, it is reasonable to wait until you are more independent and have at least one supportive person. Meanwhile, look for affirming spaces: a trusted friend, a college support group or an established community organisation, and be careful with strangers online who rush you to meet. If your mood stays low, you cannot sleep, or you think about hurting yourself, call Tele-MANAS on 14416. In an emergency call 112, or 1098 if you are under 18.
body.hg: Apne baare mein kisi ko kuch batana tumhari majboori nahi hai. Apni identity ke baare mein logon ko batana, jise aksar coming out kehte hain, tumhara apna decision hai, tumhari apni timeline pe, aur safety sabse pehle aati hai. Agar ghar ka mahaul against ho sakta hai, toh tab tak wait karna reasonable hai jab tak tum zyada independent na ho jao aur kam se kam ek supportive insaan tumhare paas na ho. Tab tak affirming spaces dhoondo: koi trusted dost, college ka support group ya koi established community organisation, aur online aise strangers se careful raho jo jaldi milne ka pressure daalein. Agar mood lagataar low rahe, neend na aaye, ya khud ko hurt karne ke thoughts aayein, toh Tele-MANAS 14416 pe call karo. Emergency mein 112 pe call karo, ya 18 se kam ho toh 1098 pe.

claim.en: LGBTQ+ people have more depression because being LGBTQ+ is itself a disorder.
claim.hg: LGBTQ+ logon mein depression zyada isliye hota hai kyunki LGBTQ+ hona khud ek disorder hai.

fact.en: The identity is not the cause. Higher distress is linked to stigma, bullying, rejection and having to hide. Where people are accepted and safe, their mental health is much closer to everyone else's.
fact.hg: Wajah identity nahi hai. Zyada distress ka connection stigma, bullying, rejection aur chhupke jeene ki majboori se hai. Jahan logon ko accept kiya jata hai aur woh safe hote hain, wahan unki mental health baaki sabke kaafi kareeb hoti hai.

takeaways.en: Everyday unequal treatment based on gender is discrimination, even when it is called tradition.
takeaways.hg: Gender ke basis pe roz ka unequal treatment discrimination hi hai, chahe use tradition bola jaye.

takeaways.en: In India same-sex relations between consenting adults are not a crime and transgender persons have legally recognised rights, though a 2026 amendment narrowing them is under challenge, and same-sex marriage is not currently recognised.
takeaways.hg: India mein consenting adults ke beech same-sex relations crime nahi hain aur transgender logon ke rights legally recognised hain, halanki inhe narrow karne wale 2026 ke amendment ko court mein challenge kiya gaya hai, aur same-sex marriage abhi recognised nahi hai.

takeaways.en: Stigma harms mental health, acceptance protects it, and help is a phone call away on 14416.
takeaways.hg: Stigma mental health ko harm karta hai, acceptance use protect karta hai, aur help 14416 pe ek call door hai.

activity.en: Map your support. Privately list three people or places where you could speak honestly about something personal, such as a friend, a relative, a teacher or a helpline. If the list is short, note one step that could add a name.
activity.hg: Apna support map banao. Privately teen aise logon ya jagahon ki list banao jahan tum kisi personal baat pe honestly bol sako, jaise koi dost, relative, teacher ya helpline. Agar list chhoti hai, toh ek aisa step likho jisse usme ek naam aur add ho sake.

q.en: What did the Supreme Court of India decide in 2018 about same-sex relationships?
q.hg: 2018 mein India ke Supreme Court ne same-sex relationships ke baare mein kya decide kiya?

options.en: Same-sex marriage became legal
options.hg: Same-sex marriage legal ho gayi

options.en: Same-sex relationships are allowed only after the age of 21
options.hg: Same-sex relationships sirf 21 saal ke baad allowed hain

options.en: The court left the old law unchanged
options.hg: Court ne purane law ko waise ka waisa rehne diya

options.en: Consensual same-sex relations between adults are not a crime
options.hg: Adults ke beech consent se bane same-sex relations crime nahi hain

explain.en: The 2018 judgment decriminalised consensual same-sex relations between adults. Marriage was a separate question, which the court declined to grant in 2023.
explain.hg: 2018 ke judgment ne adults ke beech consensual same-sex relations ko decriminalise kiya. Marriage ek alag sawaal tha, jise court ne 2023 mein recognise nahi kiya.

q.en: A person may choose not to tell anyone about their orientation or gender identity, and that is a valid choice.
q.hg: Koi insaan apni orientation ya gender identity ke baare mein kisi ko na batane ka choice kar sakta hai, aur yeh ek valid choice hai.

options.en: True
options.hg: Sahi

options.en: False
options.hg: Galat

explain.en: Coming out is personal and optional. When, how and whether to tell is for the person to decide, with safety first.
explain.hg: Coming out personal hai aur optional hai. Kab, kaise aur batana hai ya nahi, yeh wahi insaan decide karta hai, safety first ke saath.

warning.en: If you are thinking about harming yourself, or someone is threatening you or forcing 'treatment' on you because of your identity, reach out now: Tele-MANAS 14416, emergency 112, Child Helpline 1098 (under 18), Women Helpline 181.
warning.hg: Agar tumhe khud ko harm karne ke thoughts aa rahe hain, ya koi tumhari identity ki wajah se tumhe dhamka raha hai ya zabardasti 'treatment' karwa raha hai, toh abhi contact karo: Tele-MANAS 14416, emergency 112, Child Helpline 1098 (18 se kam), Women Helpline 181.

title.en: Inclusion in Practice: Words, Disability and Neurodiversity
title.hg: Inclusion Real Life Mein: Words, Disability aur Neurodiversity

subtitle.en: How to be respectful when you are not sure what to say or do
subtitle.hg: Jab samajh na aaye ki kya bolein ya karein, tab bhi respectful kaise rahein

hook.en: Inclusion is not a poster on the wall. It is who gets a seat, who gets asked, and which jokes you refuse to laugh at.
hook.hg: Inclusion deewar pe laga poster nahi hai. Inclusion yeh hai ki seat kise milti hai, kisse poocha jata hai, aur kin jokes pe tum hansne se mana kar dete ho.

objectives.en: Use respectful language about gender, orientation and disability.
objectives.hg: Gender, orientation aur disability ke baare mein respectful language use kar sako.

objectives.en: Explain why disabled and neurodivergent people need the same information and respect as everyone else.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki disabled aur neurodivergent logon ko bhi wahi information aur respect kyun chahiye jo sabko chahiye.

objectives.en: Act as an upstander when someone is bullied, while respecting differences in belief.
objectives.hg: Jab kisi ko bully kiya jaye toh uske saath khade ho sako, aur saath hi alag-alag beliefs ka respect kar sako.

body.en: Use the name and pronoun a person asks for; if you slip, say sorry once, correct yourself and move on. Use the words people use for themselves, such as gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, or the umbrella term LGBTQ+. Words like 'chhakka' or 'meetha', or 'hijra' thrown as an insult, are slurs, even when said as a joke. Do not ask a transgender or intersex person about their body or surgery; you would not ask anyone else. Never 'out' someone, meaning reveal their orientation or identity without permission. What a friend tells you in confidence stays with you, unless they are in danger and need an adult's help.
body.hg: Insaan jo naam aur pronoun apne liye bataye, wahi use karo; galti ho jaye toh ek baar sorry bolo, correct karo aur aage badho. Wahi words use karo jo log apne liye karte hain, jaise gay, lesbian, bisexual, transgender, ya umbrella term LGBTQ+. 'Chhakka' ya 'meetha' jaise words, ya gaali ki tarah phenka gaya 'hijra', slurs hain, chahe mazaak mein hi bole jayein. Kisi transgender ya intersex insaan se uski body ya surgery ke baare mein mat poocho; kisi aur se toh tum aisa nahi poochte. Kabhi kisi ko 'out' mat karo, yaani uski permission ke bina uski orientation ya identity doosron ko mat batao. Dost ne jo baat confidence mein batayi hai woh tumhare paas hi rahe, siwaye tab jab woh danger mein ho aur use kisi adult ki help chahiye.

body.en: People with physical, sensory, intellectual or psychosocial disabilities grow up with the same puberty, crushes, need for privacy and right to say no as everyone else. The common mistake is to treat them as permanent children and skip the information. That makes them less safe, not more, because someone who has never been taught about body boundaries finds it harder to recognise and report abuse. Inclusion is practical: ramps and accessible toilets, captions and sign language, material in Braille, audio or easy-read form, and speaking to the person rather than to their helper. India's Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 protects their right to equality and dignity.
body.hg: Physical, sensory, intellectual ya psychosocial disability wale log bhi usi puberty, unhi crushes, privacy ki usi zaroorat aur 'no' bolne ke usi right ke saath bade hote hain jo baaki sabke paas hai. Common galti yeh hoti hai ki unhe hamesha baccha maan liya jata hai aur information di hi nahi jaati. Isse woh zyada safe nahi, kam safe hote hain, kyunki jise body boundaries ke baare mein kabhi sikhaya hi nahi gaya, uske liye abuse ko pehchaanna aur report karna zyada mushkil hota hai. Inclusion practical cheezon se banta hai: ramps aur accessible toilets, captions aur sign language, Braille, audio ya easy-read form mein material, aur helper ki jagah seedha usi insaan se baat karna. India ka Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 unke equality aur dignity ke right ko protect karta hai.

body.en: Neurodivergent describes people whose brains work differently from the majority, for example autistic people and people with ADHD or dyslexia. It is a difference in how someone learns, senses and communicates, not a lack of intelligence or feeling. Unwritten social rules can be hard to read, so say things directly: explain what is private and what is public, what consent sounds like, and that 'maybe' or silence is not a yes. Give instructions one step at a time, allow extra processing time, and do not force eye contact or touch. If this is you, asking 'Can you say that plainly?' is a completely fair request.
body.hg: Neurodivergent un logon ko kehte hain jinka brain majority se alag tareeke se kaam karta hai, jaise autistic log aur ADHD ya dyslexia wale log. Yeh seekhne, sense karne aur communicate karne ke tareeke ka difference hai, intelligence ya feelings ki kami nahi. Society ke unwritten rules padhna mushkil ho sakta hai, isliye baat directly bolo: samjhao ki kya private hai aur kya public, consent kaisa sunai deta hai, aur yeh ki 'maybe' ya chuppi ka matlab yes nahi hota. Instructions ek-ek step karke do, process karne ke liye thoda extra time do, aur eye contact ya touch ke liye force mat karo. Agar yeh tumhare baare mein hai, toh 'Kya aap yeh seedhe words mein bol sakte ho?' poochna bilkul fair request hai.

h.en: From bystander to upstander, without erasing beliefs
h.hg: Bystander se upstander tak, beliefs mitaye bina

body.en: Bullying based on gender, orientation, caste, religion, body or disability depends on an audience. Take the audience away: do not laugh, do not forward the meme, check on the person afterwards, and report repeated harassment to a teacher, a parent or your college's complaints or anti-ragging committee. Families and faiths in India hold different views about gender and sexuality, and you may be working out your own. Respect does not require you to give up your beliefs. It requires that you do not insult, exclude, out or harm anyone. You can disagree about ideas and still treat every person with dignity.
body.hg: Gender, orientation, caste, religion, body ya disability ke basis pe hone wali bullying audience ke bharose chalti hai. Audience hata do: hanso mat, meme forward mat karo, baad mein us insaan ka haal poocho, aur baar-baar hone wali harassment ki report teacher, parent ya college ki complaints ya anti-ragging committee ko karo. India mein alag-alag families aur religions ke gender aur sexuality pe alag views hain, aur ho sakta hai tum abhi apna view bana rahe ho. Respect karne ke liye tumhe apne beliefs chhodne nahi padte. Zaroori bas itna hai ki tum kisi ko insult na karo, exclude na karo, out na karo aur harm na karo. Ideas pe disagree karke bhi har insaan ke saath dignity se pesh aaya ja sakta hai.

claim.en: Respecting LGBTQ+ people means I must give up my own culture or beliefs.
claim.hg: LGBTQ+ logon ko respect karne ka matlab hai ki mujhe apna culture ya beliefs chhodne padenge.

fact.en: Respect is about behaviour, not about agreeing on everything. You can keep your beliefs and still refuse to mock, exclude, out or hurt anyone. Equal dignity for every person is also a value written into the Indian Constitution.
fact.hg: Respect behaviour ki baat hai, har cheez pe agree karne ki nahi. Tum apne beliefs rakhte hue bhi kisi ka mazaak udane, use exclude karne, out karne ya hurt karne se mana kar sakte ho. Har insaan ki equal dignity Indian Constitution mein likhi hui value bhi hai.

takeaways.en: Use the names and words people choose for themselves, and never out anyone.
takeaways.hg: Wahi naam aur words use karo jo log apne liye choose karte hain, aur kabhi kisi ko out mat karo.

takeaways.en: Disabled and neurodivergent people have the same feelings and rights, and need information in a form that works for them.
takeaways.hg: Disabled aur neurodivergent logon ki feelings aur rights same hain, aur unhe information aise form mein chahiye jo unke kaam aaye.

takeaways.en: You can disagree with an idea and still treat every person with dignity.
takeaways.hg: Kisi idea se disagree karke bhi har insaan ke saath dignity se pesh aaya ja sakta hai.

activity.en: Audit one space you use every day, such as your classroom, tuition centre or friends' group chat. Note one thing that would make it hard for a wheelchair user, a deaf classmate, an autistic classmate or a queer classmate to take part, and one change you could suggest.
activity.hg: Roz use hone wali kisi ek space ka audit karo, jaise tumhari classroom, tuition centre ya doston ka group chat. Ek aisi cheez note karo jisse wheelchair user, deaf classmate, autistic classmate ya queer classmate ke liye wahan part lena mushkil hota ho, aur ek aisa change jo tum suggest kar sakte ho.

q.en: Your autistic classmate Ishaan does not get a sarcastic joke and asks what it means. The group starts mocking him. What is the most inclusive response?
q.hg: Tumhara autistic classmate Ishaan ek sarcastic joke nahi samajh pata aur poochta hai iska matlab kya hai. Group uska mazaak udane lagta hai. Sabse inclusive response kya hoga?

options.en: Tell Ishaan he needs to learn to take a joke
options.hg: Ishaan ko bolo ki use joke lena seekhna chahiye

options.en: Explain the joke plainly and tell the group to drop it
options.hg: Joke ka matlab seedhe words mein samjhao aur group ko bolo ki baat yahin chhod de

options.en: Stay out of it because it is not your problem
options.hg: Isse door raho kyunki yeh tumhari problem nahi hai

explain.en: A direct explanation gives Ishaan what he asked for, and telling the group to stop removes the audience that bullying depends on.
explain.hg: Direct explanation se Ishaan ko wahi milta hai jo usne poocha tha, aur group ko rokne se woh audience hat jaati hai jiske bharose bullying chalti hai.

q.en: What does it mean to 'out' someone?
q.hg: Kisi ko 'out' karne ka kya matlab hai?

options.en: Inviting them along on a group outing
options.hg: Use group outing pe invite karna

options.en: Politely asking which pronoun they use
options.hg: Politely poochna ki woh kaun-sa pronoun use karta hai

options.en: Revealing their orientation or gender identity without their permission
options.hg: Uski permission ke bina uski orientation ya gender identity doosron ko bata dena

options.en: Supporting them when they tell their family
options.hg: Jab woh apni family ko bataye toh uska saath dena

explain.en: Outing takes away a person's control over their own information and can put them at risk at home, school or work.
explain.hg: Out karne se insaan ka apni hi information pe control chhin jata hai aur woh ghar, school ya work pe risk mein pad sakta hai.

title.en: Harm Done to Bodies in the Name of Tradition
title.hg: Tradition ke Naam pe Body ko Pahunchaya Gaya Harm

subtitle.en: Female genital cutting (khatna), 'virginity tests', hymen 'repair', conversion therapy and surgery on intersex children
subtitle.hg: Female genital cutting (khatna), 'virginity test', hymen 'repair', conversion therapy aur intersex bacchon ki surgery

hook.en: Some of the deepest harm is done by people who love us and believe they are doing the right thing. Good intentions do not make a cut, a test or a 'cure' harmless.
hook.hg: Kuch sabse gehre zakhm woh log dete hain jo humse pyaar karte hain aur maante hain ki woh sahi kar rahe hain. Neeyat acchi hone se kisi cut, kisi test ya kisi 'cure' ka harm khatam nahi ho jata.

objectives.en: Describe what female genital cutting is, where it happens and why WHO calls every form of it harmful.
objectives.hg: Bata sako ki female genital cutting kya hai, kahan hoti hai aur WHO iske har form ko harmful kyun kehta hai.

objectives.en: Explain why 'virginity tests', hymen 'repair', conversion therapy and non-urgent surgery on intersex children have no medical justification.
objectives.hg: Samjha sako ki 'virginity test', hymen 'repair', conversion therapy aur intersex bacchon ki non-urgent surgery ka koi medical justification kyun nahi hai.

objectives.en: Apply the idea of bodily autonomy and know where to get help if you or someone you know is at risk.
objectives.hg: Bodily autonomy ke idea ko apply kar sako aur jaan sako ki tum ya tumhara koi jaanne wala risk mein ho toh help kahan milegi.

body.en: Female genital cutting means cutting, removing or injuring a girl's external genitals for non-medical reasons, mostly in childhood, when she cannot refuse. It ranges from cutting the clitoral hood or clitoris to, in some countries, removing labia and narrowing the vaginal opening. WHO is clear: it has no health benefit, every form is harmful, and it violates girls' and women's rights. Harms can include severe pain, bleeding, infection, scarring, painful sex, childbirth problems and lasting distress. It happens in parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia. In India it is documented mainly in the Dawoodi Bohra community, as khatna or khafz, and community women lead the campaign against it.
body.hg: Female genital cutting ka matlab hai bina kisi medical reason ke ladki ke external genitals ko kaatna, hatana ya injure karna. Iske forms clitoral hood ya clitoris ko kaatne se lekar, kuch countries mein, labia hatane aur vaginal opening ko narrow karne tak jaate hain. Yeh usually bachpan mein kiya jata hai, jab woh mana nahi kar sakti. WHO clear hai: iska koi health benefit nahi, iska har form harmful hai, aur yeh ladkiyon aur women ke rights ka violation hai. Harm mein tez dard, bleeding, infection, scarring, baad mein painful sex, childbirth mein mushkilein aur lambe time tak rehne wala distress shaamil ho sakta hai. Yeh Africa, Middle East aur Asia ke kuch hisson mein hoti hai. India mein yeh mainly Dawoodi Bohra community mein document hui hai, jahan isse khatna ya khafz kehte hain aur jahan isse khatam karne ka campaign community ki women hi lead kar rahi hain.

body.en: The hymen is a thin, stretchy rim of tissue that varies naturally between people. It may or may not tear or bleed, the first time or ever, so no examination can show whether someone has had sex. That is why WHO condemns 'virginity tests', including the 'two-finger test', which India's Supreme Court has prohibited in examinations of sexual-assault survivors. Wedding-night customs that demand blood as proof rest on the same false idea and humiliate brides. Hymen 'repair' surgery is sold on that fear. It has no health benefit, carries the risks of any operation and cannot guarantee bleeding. Nobody asks men for proof. That double standard is the real problem.
body.hg: Hymen tissue ki ek patli, stretchy rim hai jo har insaan mein naturally alag hoti hai. Woh pehli baar mein ya kabhi bhi tear ho sakti hai ya nahi bhi, bleed kar sakti hai ya nahi bhi, isliye uska koi bhi examination yeh nahi bata sakta ki kisi ne sex kiya hai ya nahi. Isi wajah se WHO 'virginity tests' ko, jisme 'two-finger test' bhi shaamil hai, condemn karta hai, aur India ke Supreme Court ne sexual assault survivors ke medical examination mein 'two-finger test' ko prohibit kiya hai. Shaadi ki raat proof ke taur pe blood maangne wale rivaaj isi galat idea pe tike hain aur dulhanon ko humiliate karte hain. Hymen 'repair' surgery isi darr ke sahare bechi jaati hai. Iska koi health benefit nahi, isme har operation jaise risks hain aur bleeding ki koi guarantee nahi. Mardon se koi proof nahi maangta. Asli problem yahi double standard hai.

body.en: Conversion therapy is any attempt to change the sexual orientation or gender identity of a person of any gender: pills, hormones, shocks, confinement, rituals, forced counselling, or a marriage arranged to 'settle' them. It cannot work, because there is no illness, and it leaves depression, shame and trauma; a doctor in India who offers it commits professional misconduct. A related harm is done to intersex children, born with natural variations in sex characteristics. Many had infant surgery only to make their genitals look typical. Such surgery is irreversible and can cause scarring, loss of sensation and infertility. Without a real medical emergency, it can wait until the person can decide.
body.hg: Conversion therapy ka matlab hai kisi insaan ki sexual orientation ya gender identity ko badalne ki koi bhi koshish: pills, hormones, shocks, band karke rakhna, rituals, zabardasti ki counselling, ya 'settle' karne ke liye arrange ki gayi shaadi. Yeh har gender ke logon ke saath kiya jata hai. Yeh kaam kar hi nahi sakti, kyunki koi illness hai hi nahi, aur peeche depression, shame aur trauma chhod jaati hai; India mein yeh offer karne wala doctor professional misconduct karta hai. Isse milta-julta harm intersex bacchon ke saath hota hai, jo sex characteristics mein natural variations ke saath paida hote hain. Bahuton ki infancy mein sirf isliye surgery kar di gayi ki unke genitals typical dikhein. Aisi surgery irreversible hai aur isse scarring, sensation ka loss aur infertility ho sakti hai. Jab tak real medical emergency na ho, yeh tab tak wait kar sakti hai jab tak woh insaan khud decide na kar sake.

h.en: Your body is not family property
h.hg: Tumhari body family ki property nahi

body.en: These practices share one pattern: adults decide something permanent about a young person's body or identity to protect family honour, marriage prospects or belonging. Most parents who do this are not cruel; they are afraid, or the same was done to them. Understanding that is not the same as accepting it. Bodily autonomy means that non-urgent, irreversible decisions about your body are yours. If you or a child you know is at risk, tell a trusted adult and call 1098 if under 18, Women Helpline 181, or 112 in danger. A doctor can treat physical effects, Tele-MANAS on 14416 supports the mind, and NALSA on 15100 offers free legal aid.
body.hg: In sab practices mein ek hi pattern hai: adults family ki izzat, shaadi ke prospects ya community mein jagah bachane ke liye kisi young insaan ki body ya identity ke baare mein koi permanent decision le lete hain. Aisa karne wale zyadatar parents cruel nahi hote; woh dare hue hote hain, ya unke saath bhi yahi hua tha. Yeh samajhna, isse accept kar lena nahi hai. Bodily autonomy ka matlab hai ki tumhari body ke aise decisions, jo urgent nahi hain aur irreversible hain, tumhe hi lene hain. Agar tum ya koi baccha jise tum jaante ho risk mein hai, toh kisi trusted adult ko batao aur 18 se kam ho toh 1098 pe, Women Helpline 181 pe, ya danger ho toh 112 pe call karo. Physical effects ka treatment doctor kar sakte hain, mind ke liye Tele-MANAS 14416 hai, aur NALSA 15100 pe free legal aid deta hai.

claim.en: If parents do something out of love and tradition, it cannot be called harm.
claim.hg: Agar parents koi kaam pyaar aur tradition ki wajah se karte hain, toh use harm nahi bol sakte.

fact.en: Harm is measured by what happens to the person, not by the intention behind it. A cut, a forced 'cure' or an unnecessary operation leaves the same pain and scars whether it was done in anger or in love. Traditions are also not fixed: many harmful customs have been changed by people from within the community itself.
fact.hg: Harm is baat se naapa jata hai ki us insaan ke saath kya hua, isse nahi ki neeyat kya thi. Koi cut, zabardasti ka 'cure' ya unnecessary operation wahi dard aur wahi scars chhodta hai, chahe woh gusse mein kiya gaya ho ya pyaar mein. Traditions fixed bhi nahi hoti: bahut se harmful rivaaj usi community ke logon ne andar se badle hain.

takeaways.en: Female genital cutting has no health benefit, and WHO treats every form of it as harm, whoever performs it.
takeaways.hg: Female genital cutting ka koi health benefit nahi hai, aur WHO iske har form ko harm maanta hai, chahe isse koi bhi kare.

takeaways.en: No test can prove virginity, no therapy can change orientation or identity, and no child needs non-urgent surgery just to look 'normal'.
takeaways.hg: Koi test virginity prove nahi kar sakta, koi therapy orientation ya identity nahi badal sakti, aur kisi bacche ko sirf 'normal' dikhne ke liye non-urgent surgery ki zaroorat nahi.

takeaways.en: You can respect a community and still refuse harm to a body; help is available on 1098, 181, 112, 14416 and 15100.
takeaways.hg: Kisi community ki respect karte hue bhi body ko harm karne se mana kiya ja sakta hai; help 1098, 181, 112, 14416 aur 15100 pe milti hai.

activity.en: Draw your own line. Privately complete this sentence in your notes: 'A decision about my body should wait for my consent when...'. Then write down one adult and one helpline you would contact if someone tried to force a procedure or a 'cure' on you or on a younger child.
activity.hg: Apni line khud draw karo. Privately apne notes mein yeh sentence complete karo: 'Meri body se jude decision ko meri consent ka wait karna chahiye, jab...'. Phir ek aise adult ka naam aur ek helpline likho jisse tum tab contact karoge jab koi tum pe ya kisi chhote bacche pe koi procedure ya 'cure' zabardasti thopne ki koshish kare.

q.en: What is WHO's position on female genital cutting when a trained health worker does it in a clean clinic?
q.hg: Jab koi trained health worker clean clinic mein female genital cutting kare, toh ispe WHO ki position kya hai?

options.en: It is acceptable because the risk of infection is lower
options.hg: Yeh theek hai kyunki infection ka risk kam hota hai

options.en: It is acceptable only if the girl is older than 15
options.hg: Yeh tabhi theek hai jab ladki 15 saal se badi ho

options.en: It is still harmful, has no health benefit and should not be done
options.hg: Yeh tab bhi harmful hai, iska koi health benefit nahi aur isse nahi kiya jana chahiye

options.en: It is recommended for hygiene
options.hg: Hygiene ke liye yeh recommend ki jaati hai

explain.en: WHO treats every form of female genital cutting as harmful and opposes health workers performing it. A clinic does not turn the removal of healthy tissue without consent into healthcare.
explain.hg: WHO female genital cutting ke har form ko harmful maanta hai aur health workers ke isse karne ka virodh karta hai. Clinic mein hone se, bina consent ke healthy tissue hatana healthcare nahi ban jata.

q.en: Your cousin Ritu, 22, says her future in-laws want a doctor's 'virginity certificate' before the wedding. She is frightened. What is the most helpful response?
q.hg: Tumhari 22 saal ki cousin Ritu batati hai ki uske hone wale in-laws shaadi se pehle doctor ka 'virginity certificate' chahte hain. Woh dari hui hai. Sabse helpful response kya hoga?

options.en: Suggest she gets the test done quickly so the matter ends
options.hg: Suggest karna ki woh jaldi se test karwa le taaki baat khatam ho

options.en: Tell her no examination can show this, that such tests are unscientific and she can refuse, and offer to stand with her or call 181
options.hg: Use batana ki koi examination yeh nahi dikha sakta, aise tests unscientific hain aur woh mana kar sakti hai, aur uske saath khade rehne ya 181 pe call karne ka offer dena

options.en: Advise hymen 'repair' surgery so that she is safe either way
options.hg: Hymen 'repair' surgery ki advice dena taaki woh har haal mein safe rahe

explain.en: The hymen cannot show whether someone has had sex, so a 'virginity certificate' is medically meaningless and the test itself is degrading. Accurate facts and someone on her side help more than going along with it.
explain.hg: Hymen yeh nahi dikha sakta ki kisi ne sex kiya hai ya nahi, isliye 'virginity certificate' ka medically koi matlab nahi hai aur yeh test khud degrading hai. Sahi facts aur kisi ka uske side mein khada hona, chupchaap maan lene se zyada help karta hai.

warning.en: If someone is being cut, confined, or forced into a 'cure', an examination, surgery or marriage, treat it as an emergency: call 112, Child Helpline 1098 (under 18) or Women Helpline 181. Heavy bleeding, fever or severe pain after any cutting or surgery needs a hospital immediately. Legal points here are a plain-language summary, not legal advice.
warning.hg: Agar kisi ko cut kiya ja raha hai, band rakha ja raha hai, ya kisi 'cure', examination, surgery ya shaadi ke liye force kiya ja raha hai, toh isse emergency samjho: 112, Child Helpline 1098 (18 se kam) ya Women Helpline 181 pe call karo. Kisi bhi cutting ya surgery ke baad heavy bleeding, bukhaar ya tez dard ho toh turant hospital jao. Yahan di gayi legal baatein plain-language summary hain, legal advice nahi.
